\section[la música]{la música — another art of the Muses}

\label{lesson:ES-C413-musica}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{el museo}, a place whose name once meant a seat of the Muses. Their art also gives Spanish \textbf{la música}.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
Greek \textbf{mousik\'{\={e}}}, the art of the Muses, travelled into Latin \textbf{mūsica} and then Spanish \textbf{música}. English \textbf{music} followed the same road through French. The root is already anchored in \textbf{museo}, so this lesson extends that family rather than assigning it a second owner.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: the written accent}]
The stress falls on the first beat: \textbf{MÚ-si-ca}. Spanish writes the accent because that antepenultimate stress must always be marked. The noun is feminine: \textbf{la música}, \textbf{música clásica}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{la música}
  \item \emph{música clásica}
  \item \emph{me gusta la música}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Music? (\emph{La música}.) Classical music? (\emph{Música clásica}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/m\%C3\%BAsica}{DLE: música}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[el concierto]{el concierto — music brought together}

\label{lesson:ES-C413-concierto}



\begin{quote}
Recall \textbf{la música}. A scheduled event where people perform music is \textbf{el concierto}.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{Concierto} belongs to \textbf{concertar}, to bring things into agreement, from Latin \textbf{concertāre}. Italian and French helped the musical event-sense travel, and English \textbf{concert} is a close relative. Think of performers bringing their parts together.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={Grammar Lens: concert of what?}]
Use \textbf{de} to name the kind: \textbf{un concierto de música clásica}. The event is masculine: \textbf{el concierto}, \textbf{un concierto}.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{el concierto}
  \item \emph{un concierto de música}
  \item \emph{un concierto de música clásica}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Concert? (\emph{El concierto}.)

Source: \href{https://dle.rae.es/concierto}{DLE: concierto}.
\end{tcolorbox}

\section[(review)]{music recall two — choose the Saturday-night event}

\label{lesson:ES-C413-music-recall-2}



\begin{quote}
Someone likes music and wants to go out on Saturday night.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item “Jorge likes music.” {[}YOU SAY: \emph{A Jorge le gusta la música.}{]}
  \item “There is a classical music concert on Saturday.” {[}YOU SAY: \emph{Hay un concierto de música clásica el sábado.}{]}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Which event matches the Saturday-night plan? (\emph{El concierto de música clásica}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
